title: When two truths collide
subtitle: Hold both sides without choosing — and let a third thing surface.

steps.body:
Some of the hardest things to hold are two truths that don't agree.

We're not here to pick a winner, or to talk you out of either one. We're here to hold both at once — and see what a third thing might be, in its own time.

steps.title: One side of you pulls toward…
steps.body: A wish, a fear, a direction. Say it plainly.

steps.title: And another side knows, or wants, the opposite.
steps.body: Not the 'should' — the other true thing.

steps.title: How much tension is in holding both?
steps.body: Just a read on where you are.
That pull has some weight. One breath — you don't have to resolve anything here.
Now hold both at once, if you can. Don't choose. Let them both be true for a moment, side by side.

steps.title: Is there anything that wants to emerge between them?
steps.body: Don't force it. A third thing — an image, a small move, a 'what if' — that isn't either side. Or leave it blank; it often comes later.

exit.body: You held both sides without collapsing one into the other. That's the practice — the third thing comes in its own time, not on demand.
